headline: UN Counts 302 New Kachin Mine Sites
deck: OHCHR said satellite images confirmed 302 new rare-earth sites in Kachin since 2021, a 149 percent increase, and Shan sites up from 12 before the coup to 85 after. The press release finds transboundary pollution from mining runoff. It does not name buyers. Civilian-death totals in the same-day wire are not printed in the OHCHR note.
body: The UN human rights office published a 25 August press release on report A/HRC/63/21, covering 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2026 [E1][E2]. The title on the OHCHR page is that the human rights situation in Myanmar has plummeted to a new low amid unrelenting violations and unregulated exploitation of natural resources [E1]. The advance unedited report page is the companion document [E2]. The full PDF body was not retrieved before the freeze [E1][E2].

Mine counts are in the press release itself. Satellite images, it said, confirmed that Kachin remained the primary mining area, with 302 new sites since 2021, a 149 percent increase [E1]. In Shan, sites increased from 12 pre-coup to 85 post-coup [E1]. Findings indicated a peak in trade flows in 2023 amounting to USD 1.4 billion, with limited official records [E1]. Massive volumes of hazardous leaching agents and toxic mining runoff flow directly into local waterways, resulting in severe chemical and transboundary pollution [E1].

Thailand is not named in the extracted OHCHR press text [E1]. The press release attributes the illicit economy to a complex web of actors and does not name controllers or buyers [E1]. Civilian killed, IDP and hunger totals that circulated on the wires are not in the OHCHR press extract used here [E1].

The reportable 25 August ledger is the satellite mine count and the transboundary-pollution finding, not a reconstructed death toll from a wire [E1]. Whether a later UN product names commercial end-buyers is a later clock [E1][E2].
